text: Why is the Collatz loop included in a chapter about termination?
choices: It is an example of an infinite loop
Whether it always halts is an unproved open problem, showing termination can be genuinely hard
Its invariant is unusually difficult to state
explanation: Six lines, posed in 1937, verified by computer to about 2^68, and unproved. If deciding whether that loop halts is beyond us, you might guess that deciding it for arbitrary programs is beyond any method — which Turing proved in 1936.
